chapter: Les Hite, Sebastian's and Duke Ellington
title: Forming the Hampton and Basie bands without reward; winding down
summary: Royal resents that he built Hampton's band and Basie's 1950s band without reward, and now wants only recordings and television work.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Was he running the finances or was Gladys running the finances? (inaudible)?

Oh, yes. After all, it was his band. When your wife is running the finances, you got to say something about it. You know, you can't duck under too many skirts always, you know. People always try to find out different reasons why certain things don't happen. They can find excuses. But I formed his big band, put it together. He became a millionaire. Then, when I was in the service, after I left his band, he never even came by to take me out to dinner and I put his band together for him.
So, that's a little salt in the wounds sometimes. But that's unimportant, because those things have gone past. I also

formed the Count Basie Big Band of the '50s and he recouped his riches again and I didn't get none of that bread, which is still all right, too, because I got good health and I'm still able to laugh and I'm not really bitter about it at all because it's impossible to starve a man to death that has enough intestinal fortitude to fight this big old nasty world and I've got it. I intend to keep on doing what I have to do for a couple more years and I'll --

Oh, you know, I'll take it a little easy. I sort of take things a little easier as it is now. I don't really like to do anything now except make recordings and TV jobs which pay well with short hours. That's what I would like to do for the rest of my life, so far as my working days are concerned. So far as going out and whooping and hollering and stomping my feet and doing that, I hope to never do that again as long as I live because I've proven my point a long time ago.
